summary: The note describes the United Defense M42, a weapon originally intended for U.S. troops that instead became more popular as an air-dropped arm for partisan forces in occupied Europe. It was supplied to British-led partisans on Crete, used by Italian and French Resistance groups, passed to Dai Li's resistance forces in China, and issued to Filipino troops and guerrillas during and after World War II. The note also explains that its 9 mm caliber let resistance fighters use captured ammunition, reducing the need for repeated resupply drops.
one_line: The United Defense M42 was a weapon designed for U.S. troops that was widely air-dropped to resistance forces across Europe, China and the Philippines in World War II.
key_facts: The United Defense M42 was intended for use by U.S. troops at the time of its design.
The United Defense M42 found more favor being air-dropped to partisan forces in occupied Europe than with its intended users.
The weapon was air dropped to supply British-led partisan forces on the island of Crete, where it was used extensively.
The United Defense M42 also saw use among the partisan forces of the Italian and French Resistance.
Some United Defense M42 weapons were transferred to Dai Li's regular resistance forces in China for use against the Japanese invasion.
The United Defense M42 was issued for use by Filipino troops under the Philippine Army and Philippine Constabulary during World War II.
Filipino issue of the United Defense M42 continued from 1942 through the Post-World War II era until the 1960s.
The United Defense M42 was used by local recognized guerrillas in the Philippines from 1942 to 1945 during the Japanese Occupation.
The United Defense M42 used 9 mm caliber ammunition.
The 9 mm caliber allowed resistance forces to use captured ammunition in their weapons.
Using captured ammunition eliminated the need for repeated re-supply drops to resistance forces.
